title: Evaluating the Security of Logic Locking on Deep Neural Networks
problem: Logic locking schemes like HPNN are proposed to protect DNN model parameters using hardware root-of-trust, but their actual security against sophisticated I/O attacks remains unproven. This paper investigates whether such schemes can be broken by extracting secret keys from the network.
motivation: Model piracy and adversarial attacks pose significant threats when malicious users have access to DNN model parameters, making rigorous security evaluation of protection mechanisms critical.
method: The attack extracts the secret key that protects a neural network by observing how the network responds to different inputs and outputs—a technique called an I/O attack. It combines two mathematical approaches: algebraic methods (solving systems of equations for the key) and learning-based methods (training a model to infer the key from input-output patterns). The attack reconstructs the key piece by piece, minimizing how many test inputs are needed, and verifies each piece to ensure correctness. This approach was successfully demonstrated on large neural networks with complex architectures.
key_novelty: An incremental I/O attack combining algebraic and learning-based methods can extract logic-locking keys from neural networks with minimal test inputs.
contributions: Presents a combined algebraic and learning-based I/O attack against logic-locked DNNs
Demonstrates that HPNN-style logic locking is insecure on large networks with complex architectures
Develops rigorous key extraction verification procedures with demonstrated accuracy and efficiency
Shows foreseeable variants of HPNN are also vulnerable to the proposed attack

metrics.accuracy: Key extraction accuracy and attack success rate

limitations: Limitations are not discussed in the provided abstract.
